name: Barkos
title: Temple Servant After the Exile
summary: Barkos was the ancestor of one of the families among the temple servants (netinim) who returned from the Babylonian exile to Jerusalem. He is mentioned in the lists of returnees in both the book of Ezra and the book of Nehemiah. His descendants served at the temple in Jerusalem after its rebuilding.

keyEvents.title: Listed Among the Temple Servants in the Book of Ezra
keyEvents.description: Barkos' descendants are mentioned among the temple servants (netinim) who returned from Babylon to Jerusalem under Zerubbabel's leadership.

keyEvents.title: Listed Among the Temple Servants in the Book of Nehemiah
keyEvents.description: Barkos' descendants are again listed in the parallel record of returnees from exile in the book of Nehemiah.

keyEvents.title: The Return from Babylon
keyEvents.description: The families of the temple servants, including Barkos' descendants, were among those who could prove their Israelite ancestry and participated in rebuilding the temple and the community in Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: The Role of Temple Servants in the Rebuilt Community
keyEvents.description: The temple servants (netinim), to whom Barkos' descendants belonged, were assigned specific duties in service at God's house in Jerusalem after the exile.
